title: Alex Wang on What China Gets Right — and Wrong — on the Environment - The Wire China
gist: UCLA law professor Alex Wang, who holds a US-China relations chair and co-directs the Emmett Institute on Climate Change, built his expertise on Chinese environmental governance through a 2004 Fulbright and six years running the Natural Resources Defense Council's Beijing environmental law program.

insights.claim: Alex Wang is a UCLA School of Law professor holding the Walter and Shirley Wang Chair in U.S.-China Relations and Communications and co-directing the Emmett Institute on Climate Change and the Environment, with a research focus on the law and politics of Chinese environmental governance.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
entities: Emmett Institute on Climate Change and the Environment
insights.so_what: Identifies a named academic authority on Chinese environmental law/governance worth tracking for informed commentary on China's climate and environmental regulatory trajectory.
insights.quote: Alex Wang is a Professor of Law at UCLA School of Law, where he holds the Walter and Shirley Wang Chair in U.S.-China Relations and Communications and co-directs the Emmett Institute on Climate Change and the Environment.

insights.claim: Wang first engaged with China's environmental sector on a Fulbright grant in 2004, then spent six years at the Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC) in Beijing building its environmental law and governance program.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Points to NRDC's Beijing office as a long-running channel through which U.S. environmental-law expertise was embedded into Chinese environmental governance capacity-building, relevant context for how much of China's environmental legal framework has foreign-NGO fingerprints.
insights.quote: He first went to China on a Fulbright grant in 2004, then spent six years at the Natural Resources Defense Council in Beijing, building the organization's environmental law and governance program
